top5.title: Trump and Silicon Valley convinced Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back
top5.description: The article explains how Donald Trump and Silicon Valley pushed Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back.
top5.why: The reported political and Silicon Valley pressure on Nvidia’s leadership signals potentially significant implications for the company’s strategy, valuation, and U.S. technology policy.

top5.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
top5.description: CrowdStrike announced the all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, bringing together endpoint protection, zero-trust networking, cloud security and threat intelligence. Jay Chaudhry will remain CEO of Zscaler and join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.
top5.why: CrowdStrike’s proposed $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler would reshape the cybersecurity market by combining endpoint, cloud, identity, and zero-trust capabilities.

top5.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to automate code approvals
top5.description: Claude Ship brings together agents that can review code, fix issues, and automatically approve certain changes. The service is being rolled out in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise plans on GitHub repositories.
top5.why: Anthropic’s Claude Ship moves AI coding agents closer to autonomous software delivery by letting them review, fix, and approve code within enterprise GitHub workflows.

top5.title: The EU Chips Act Unlocks €33 Billion in Investment
top5.description: Europe has unlocked €33 billion to revive its semiconductor industry, with new factories, GaN power-production sites, and packaging and testing lines spread across more than 20 projects. However, commercial production will not begin immediately.
top5.why: The EU Chips Act’s €33 billion investment package materially strengthens Europe’s semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, and power-electronics capacity.

top5.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist calls for limiting the pace of AI progress
top5.description: Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores for every major model since GPT-3.5 and is asking competing labs to agree on common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.
top5.why: OpenAI’s chief scientist calling for common limits on the pace of AI progress elevates frontier-model safety from an internal concern to a potential industry-wide governance issue.
